entry.title: Masters applications
entry.content:
Hello everyone, this is a blog explaining my experience during the masters application for Fall 2026. I will be joining University of California San Diego for my Masters of Science in Data Science from Fall 2026.

It was the end of third year, coming back to India from my exchange program and starting my internship at JLR. Although the internship was pretty good, the work was slightly saturated and didn’t see enough growth in career or other aspects after discussing with many people. This influenced my decision of pursuing a masters degree abroad for a rich academic experience and possible career prospects. (Also my sister was in the US, which slightly influenced my decision). I decided to lock in and start MS application prep towards the end of my internship in early July of 2025.

I mostly contacted a couple of seniors, grad mentors, grad booklet by ugac for advice and grad resources. I also followed the amazing blogs by Kalpesh Krishna for GRE and ToEFL advice, along with casual reddit gyan.

General Timeline

  • July End: Start shortlisting universities and countries and finalise on which ones need GRE / ToEFL / any other exams. The shortlisted universities could incur changes again and again.
  • September 1st week: Get done with GRE atleast.
  • September 2nd week: Get done with ToEFL / other exams and Start with CV
  • September 3rd week: Start requesting professors / companies for LORs and start drafting rough SOP and LORs.
  • October end: Clear picture of your LOR professors and SOP.
  • November 2nd week: Start all the application links, fill them and submit soon.

These timelines might shift if you are also applying for Placements / can get shifted due to midsems etc.

Things needed for the application

Firstly your application majorly depends on your cpi (I know people with 8-8.5 cpi as well who got MS admits), SOP and LORs. Some universities have a requirement of undergraduate courses to be completed. You can show that in the form of courses done / similar courses done during your stay at IITB. It’s generally hard to tell what was the reason for a university to accept since their rejection mails are quite standard.

Shortlisting University

I decided to apply for about 11 universities with 4 hard, 4 medium and 3 easy. Multiple factors can influence your decision for a university. Things like advice from seniors, interested department, qs ranking, labs and research groups, Weather, Cost of living, TA-RA opportunities for possible funding and overall Job Market. You can consider these factors including some more like relatives in foreign country / how accessible it will be for your parents to visit - for shortlisting countries as well. These decisions along with having an idea of education in KTH (European univ) led to choosing US for most of the universities and Canada for a university. Rejected UK / europe / Australia / NZ and other places due to these factors.

I applied to following universities in the following programs, ranked from hardest to easiest for me:

  1. Carenige Mellon University, PhD in Stats and Data Science
  2. New York Universty, PhD in Data Science
  3. University of Michigan - Ann Arbor, PhD in Industrial and Operations Engineering
  4. University of Illinois - Urbana Champaign, MS in Statistic and Analytics
  5. University of Texas - Austin, MS in ECE, DICE track
  6. Georgia Tech - Atlanta, MS in Computational Science and Engineering
  7. University of California - San Diego, MS in Data Science
  8. University of Wisconsin - Madison, MS in Computer Science
  9. University of Waterloo - Canada
  10. Northwestern University, MS in Stats and Data Science
  11. Texas A&M University, MS in CS with AI

Note that both NYU PhD and UMich PhD had an option where they would consider my application for a masters degree if PhD doesn’t qualify as a good fit.

Details about crafting an SOP

  • First paragraph - general / overall interest in the field, why do you want to pursue it, brief idea about what you would do in the future and how the corresponding Masters / PhD degree will help here.
  • Second paragraph to penultimate paragraph - Take 2-3 projects (that includes LOR preferably) and explain them very well. don’t go into too much of technicalities, explain it briefly and how it shaped your interest in the field. Be as specific as possible. Being specific gives an idea to the institute that you are very clear about your goals and interests and hence you are pursuing higher studies. Being specific is weighted more in a PhD application as compared to Masters application though.
  • Final paragraph (different for diff univ) - explain which courses / labs / professors you are interested in working with and why, and hence this degree in this institute will be helpful. Make sure to mention the prof that you want to be your advisor in the case of PhD application. The profs will surely evaluate your application in that case.

Note that all the paragraphs except for the last one, can be common for all universities (except for First para saying “I’m interested in ___ degree in ___ instutute).

Write your SOPs in Latex, it will look good. Mention your email address and website link as well in the top, again this will look good. Use a simple looking template for SOP with good enough margin space etc. I like to use a font similar to Times New Roman. Generally keep SOP as 1.5 to 2 pages. It doesn’t need to be from end to end or filling entire page.

I used this template for my SOP.

Details about LORs

Generally universities ask for 3 LORs, with >= 2 Academic LORs (can be TA / Research work / grades - slightly weaker) and <= 1 industry LOR (better if you did research work there). Professors and industry people generally don’t have enough time to draft an LOR. So you can go ahead, draft an LOR and send the professor. They will generally make some minor changes, sign it and submit it to the university. MAKE SURE TO WAIVE THE RIGHTS TO VIEW THE LOR DOCUMENT. Not waving the same will give bad impression for the professor and for the admitting institute. And ask the professors / industry to send it with a header / seal and with official email id.

You are free to exaggerate since you will write the draft (don’t do it too much) and make sure to say that you were very helpful in the project because of this aspect and these technical skills. This phrasing will generally stand out. Can write them in Google Doc itself.

Details about CV

CV is not very important for Masters application but it is extremely important for a PhD application. The Professors will keep your CV and take your inteview in case of the latter. Don’t make it like a normal IITB placement / internship resume. You are not expected to do GPT and write lines such that it covers end to end of a line and span only 1 line / 2 line. There are no such restrictions. The CV doesn’t need to be only 2 page or something. Can have more than 2 pages. Start with your name, contact, location etc. Then keep sections like this: Education, Research Interests, Publications and/or patents and/or conferences you attended (if any), Scholastic achievements (can be later if projects are better), Research Projects, Technical Skills, Teaching experience, Relevant courses, Extracurriculars & community service.

It is recommended to use Latex for CV. I used this template for my CV (minus the photo).

Preparing for exams

GRE: Take the GRE General test. Math part was easy, just be accurate. For the english part, I took Gregmat subscription for about 2 months and did words / paragraphs and other questions from there. It was pretty helpful. End of the day, you need to memorise as many words as possible (about 600 words ideally). I used Barrons 333, Flashcards by Magoosh and Gregmat’s 800 word list. For questions, keep on practicing with the officials books and big book. The official GRE website has 2 sample mock tests. They are actual GRE level tests tbh. The first one is untimed and second one is timed. Take the first one few days before the test (like 2 weeks) and second test about 5 days before the test. The rest of the mock tests were from Gregmat. This exam needs atleast 1 - 1.5 month preparation if you don’t read novels / write blogs multiple times. (I personally hated GRE :/). There is some chinese websites like this where you can take free mock tests from.

ToEFL: This was easy, has 4 sections - Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking. Take some mock tests and you will be good to go (approx 4-5 days prep time is good enough). Took mocktests from Testglider

Other important documents

Latest Transcript, Passport which is pretty recent (else it might cause issues during visa / stay in the foreign country), 10th 12th markscard, Exchange transcript (if any).

Application Decisions

PhD interviews start to come by Jan start and can go until February Mid. One gets PhD decisions during that time only. Only after that one gets Masters decisions. I started getting my rejections from February itself and going upto April End. My UCSD MS DS accept was in Feb 3rd week, NYU MS DS accept was in March 1st week and UMich MS IOE accept was in April End. I chose UCSD MS DS out of the three options.

Specifically for US universities & for international students

There are a couple of things to do once you get an admit and choose a particular university.

  1. Accept the university that you are interested in. For some of them, you gave to pay some deposit to accept it.
  2. Start finding for a Loan from and bank, generally HDFC Credilla, Leap Finance, IDFC bank etc works. Better to take loan in INR since repayment will be better (due to INR to USD depreciation)
  3. Once you get your loan sanctioned, request for i20 from the university. The i20 will have approximate cost for 1 year in that institute. Getting i20 depends on the university. Generally it takes 2-3 weeks. I was extremely lucky and got it in one day lol.
  4. Once you get i20, start filling DS160 form, submit it along with SEVIS number, start applying for appointments in US visa scheduling website here.
  5. Parallely, pay the mandatory $350 SEVIS fee for all students in this and print this i901 form.
  6. Give biometrics, during interview day, get ready with DS160 submission document, sevis fee paid receipt (1901 basically), visa appointment email printout, passport, loan documents, i20 and acceptance letter. Your visa decision will come up in couple of days and if approved you can pick it up there in the consulate or ask them to courier it to your address for extra fees of about 1000 INR.
  7. Book flights and go to the US!

Conclusion

Be confident, masters/phd applications will be slightly intensive but you will go through this phase. Whatever work you have done for past couple of years before the applications will certainly help you build a strong application for your higher studies. Contact me if you have more queries. All the best for your future!
entry.summary: Suggestions and experience of my Masters applications

entry.title: Exchange Process
entry.content:
Hi there, this is a blog explaining my experience for applying to an exchange program via IIT Bombay. I went to an exchange program in KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden from Jan’25 till May’25 for Spring semester of 2024-25 Academic year.

I wanted to gain some academic & research experience in a foerign university (along with visiting europe lol). Hence I thought of applying for an exchange program. I ruled out 7th sem because of Placement season / masters application, ruled out 8th sem because last semester with friends. Hence thought of applying for 6th semester only.

I was balancing both intern season and semex application, the former being much more intensive :/ (it’s okay, you guys will get through this). Here is a rough procedure for semester exchange.

Rough things needed

Unlike Masters application and all, you do not need any SOP / LOR / CV etc for Exchange. Exchange is determined only by your CPI and Branch and your preference. Nothing else is generally required.

Some things to note is that French university students can get CHARPAK scholarship, Swiss university students can also avail scholarship and I’ve heard Aalto university paying their students if you do an RA under them. Keeping these in mind, lets get into the details. Also IIT Bombay doesn’t send students to german universities since their academic semester have a huge overlap, leading to missing out on a lot of classes.

Shortlisting University and Mapping courses

As soon as the email was received from the IR office, I started shortlisting the universities. Based on my CPI range and branch, I could know which universities are good enough for me to apply and I could evaluate my chances based on that. Mapping courses is arguably the most stressful / time-consuming / logistical nightmare step during an exchange.

One has to map all the courses that they are interested to do in the foreign university. Say one needs to do 5 courses abroad. Then they need to search their version of “internal asc”, and check which course run for the given semester based on it’s previous occurances. So if you are going in the Spring 2027, then check Spring 2026, 2025, 2024 etc courses in the foreign university and then do the mapping. It can be mapped to either a Spring / Autumn course at IIT Bombay; there is no such restriction of mapping spring courses of exchange univ to spring courses of iitb only. Because of this, one has to generally go ahead and map 8-9 courses per university.

Depending on the department, one has to or doesn’t need to take signature from course instructor of iitb. In mechanical department, I had to take sign from all the course instructors. This is not the case in Energy dept / Math dept etc. So if one is applying for say 5 universities for semex, one can expect like 2-3 signatures per professor for 15-17 different professors. This becomes a nightmare if you miss out on some of them. So I would recommended you to make an excel sheet and keep on updating whether you have made mapping -> the instructor has signed -> all courses signed for that institute etc.

You can get the signs either by going to their cabin or uploading it in AMS. If you haven’t heard of AMS, it is an online application management system where professors can digitally sign the document that you have uploaded. The professors get an email to sign the document as soon as you request the signature. So it is recommended for you to combine all the documents that needs to be signed by a particular professor and ask the signature only once, so that they won’t get flooded with different emails for same/different courses of different institutes.

About 50% of the times, professors sign the document without any reminder, 20% of the times, you have to remind them and sign, the rest 30% ask you to bring a physical printed sheet and then they give a physical signature for the same. Some professors are slightly annoying and they wont sign the course. I would recommended you to skip these professors and focus on other courses. These issues generally arise when you ask mapping for a core course, which generally requires a DUGC meeting for approval (most likely reject but people have tried and succeded).

I would recommend one to start the process as soon as possible since mapping takes a good amount of time. Keep atleast 10 working days for the mapping and signature process to be done. So one can decide their timeline based on this.

Once done, you just have to take facad signature (AMS possible here) and then HOD signature (physical signature only allowed in most departments) and submit it to the International Relations (IR) office at IIT Bombay main building, in the first floor. Do this before the deadline for that particular university and give a preference.

Generally the IITB deadlines for different universities are in 3 different dates. First ones for good european univs and NUS (like ETH Zurich and NUS etc), second one covering most other good universities, third one covering universities like PoliMi etc. Lets call this Deadline A, B and C respectively. You have to submit these applications for all the univs you are interested in, before the corresponding deadline. Say you are close to deadline A, and you filled ETHZ, NUS etc and gave a preference. If you get ETHZ (say), then you won’t be able to apply for any more universities correspinding to deadline B and C and you have to accept the decision asap. But if you do-not get this university in deadline A, you can apply for deadline B univs and repeat the same process.

Once you get a university, Congratulations! you are halfway (or more) done with the semester exchange process. I remeber applying to ETH Zurich, EPFL, NUS, KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Denmark Technical University (DTU).

After getting a university

After you get a university, IR office will ask you to do the following

  • some formalities of filling an applcation & giving details
  • then you get an acceptance letter (this includes health insurance for the stay of the semester as well)
  • apply for housing in their oncampus website / search offcampus housing
  • start visa application once you get the acceptance letter, generally though VFS global / embassy visit in Delhi or Mumbai.

Specifically for KTH Sweden

I filled the official exchange application for KTH and their housing. I got housing offer i think by october. My preferences was Lappis > Teknikringen > other options. Lappis is the student housing village in Stockholm, its cheaper but about 4-5 km away & connected through public transport. Teknikringen is oncampus housing and hence you can walk to all places. I ended up getting Teknikringen.

I got their acceptance letter by October 3rd week. Unfortunately, VFS won’t take Residence Permit application for Sweden. And I did not have to apply for a Schengen visa first and get RP there once arriving in the country. The good thing was that there was no appointment to be booked for biometrics at Swedish embassy. So I just called them and got to know their availability and timings (I think RP applications were open only from 8:30AM to 10:30AM, confirm before proceeding!). Once I was sure, I booked the flights to delhi, presented acceptance letter, financial docs and passport to the embassy and gave fingerprint. They confirmed my application, said my RP was confimed in 2-3 days and they said it will be sent to the delhi consulate within a month. I chose an option to send it to mumbai consulate (closer to South India) for some extra fee (I think 500 rupees extra, cash provided during embassy visit). Once RP was confirmed, I booked the flight for Sweden by November 1st week. I received the RP by December 15th and went to Stockholm on 10th January 2025 by AirFrance.

Finances: 90% of Travel to and from Mumbai-Stockholm and RP was covered by IITB’s Institute of Eminence fund (similar to conference travel). I had to pay standard IITB tution for 6th semester, did not have to pay mess/hostel fees. Rest all expenses including stay in Europe, food, rent, travel there was supposed to covered by the same person (unless you get a scholarship that will assist this)

Courses at KTH was pretty assignments heavy as compared to the ones in IITB. Nevertheless they were good ans intellectually stimulating. You could say about 10 hours of academic load other than classes for the semester. The language of instruction was English. One is only allowed to map courses taught in English also. Language was not an issue in Sweden, everyone knows English. This might be an issue in France / Switzerland or Italy though.

Sweden is a pretty cold place, so pack your bags with enough cold clothes to survive in winters of -10 degC and have fun in europe! All the best for yoir exchange application and make sure to contact me if you need any help!
